strategyPosture: Hold the rotation read and probe, don't chase: the index is priced for calm while leadership churns underneath, so new risk goes only to fundamental-vs-price gaps with verified theses (AVGO, BWXT), not to the month's ripping narrative names.

themes.counterRead: The risk is misreading rotation as safety: if HY OAS widens past ~4.5% or lending standards tighten, this same setup becomes a rollover and the index-level calm offers no protection. Until then, the correct posture is selective, not defensive.
themes.dataAnchor: SPY sits 2.0% off its 52-week high while the Mag7 average is 11.5% off theirs (divergence gap -9.54 pts); IWM is -6.9% over 3 months. Credit shows no stress: HY OAS 3.12 (tight), SLOOS bank lending standards at 0% (loose, far below the ~40% stress threshold), VIX 16.38. The 2s10s curve is +36bps — normalized, not inverted.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The market believes the tape is healthy: SPY near highs, QQQ +5.1% over the last month, VIX pinned at 16.4 — a benign grind higher into Q4.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS widening above 4.5% or SLOOS moving off 0% — either flips this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: The template decline classifier labels all of these SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, but it cannot see guidance trajectory — APP carries a September 2026 class action and TTD was removed from the S&P 500 on Sep 21 after guiding revenue decline. Those two are possible value traps, not sentiment discounts. AVGO and BWXT have the cleanest verified gaps; APP needs the legal overhang resolved before sizing.

themes.narrative: The market believes enterprise software and AI-adjacent names are broken — six straight months of multiple compression pricing them as ex-growth.
themes.watchFor: AVGO or BWXT reclaiming momentum entry triggers, or any guidance cut that converts a sentiment discount into a fundamental short.

themes.counterRead: The suppliers of the actual electrons trade at troughs: VST -35.6% (insiders bought $1.17M at the trough) and BWXT -43.4%, both promoted to the opportunity watchlist on nuclear-power demand. If the AI-power demand thesis is real, the mispricing is in the suppliers, not the hyperscalers — chase META here and you're paying for a story the suppliers don't confirm.
themes.dataAnchor: META +25.5% over the last month (top 1-month leader in the tracked set); GEV +9.9% 1m and +3.8% today; PWR +8.7% 1m. Against that: VST -35.6% from highs, BWXT -43.4% — the nuclear/power suppliers sit at cyclical troughs while the narrative names rip.
themes.label: AI-power narrative running hot
themes.narrative: The market believes AI power demand is a straight line up and is paying up for the obvious beneficiaries — META's 25% month is the poster child.
themes.watchFor: VST/BWXT breaking down further on no news (thesis intact, better entry) vs a META reversal on heavy volume (narrative exhaustion).

themes.counterRead: There is no fundamental anchor for this leg in today's data — it's pure risk-on flow. For Jun's book specifically: BMNR is already a 14%-of-Core overweight up ~38% from cost; a +14.7% month on top of that is a reason to re-check position sizing discipline, not to add. The standing decision (no trim, no stop) holds, but the concentration deserves eyes, not autopilot.
